verdictOnCurrentFilms: All three are one template in three costumes, which is exactly the nostalgia-as-a-filter I exist to challenge. Same recipe every time: the archive image is blurred, enlarged and smeared behind itself as a muddy amber/grey/gold wash (Douglass frames 1, 5, 6; Persia frames 4-6 where the glow is amber, not lapis), a small plate floats top-centre with huge dead ground either side, and a rounded translucent black box of default Times/Georgia caption sits on top. The caption box overlaps the plate in at least a third of frames (Douglass title page, Persia seal and stele, Ford Highland Park) so the evidence is covered by the subtitle. Nothing is a system: pairs of frames nine seconds apart are identical (Ford 2/3, Douglass 5/6, Persia 4/5), the only 'motion' is a generic fade to black (Douglass frame 3 fades photo and caption together like a slideshow). No exhibit type anywhere: no Anton, Abril Fatface, Cormorant, Fraunces; no red-orange, gold-on-iron-gall, lapis or madder; no Syriac, Chinese, Urdu. The RECONSTRUCTION label is 9px grey text in the top-right corner, so painted frames (Ford farmhouse, Persia hall) read as full-bleed cinema with no honest marker; credits are unreadable on a TV. The blurred-backdrop trick also quietly re-grades the evidence (the Douglass 1855 engraving sits on grey fog, the title page on mustard). Good bones to keep: the faceless/back-turned paintings (boy at the bench, rider on Bagley Avenue), the ungraded Highland Park photograph, the seal, the title page. Everything else is a slideshow with subtitles, not a film touched by any council.
concept: THE PLATE ENGINE: each film is a deterministic system with one rule taken from its exhibit's own metaphor, and every title, caption, transition and graphic is an output of that rule driven by the narration's word timestamps, not hand-keyed. Douglass obeys the composing stick (every line is set, justified to one measure and pulled as a proof), Ford obeys the line (constant pitch and takt, one station per beat), Persia obeys the road (one continuous route polyline the camera travels), Partition obeys the line that cuts (one drawn line that divides type, plates and screen and never retreats). Shared across all four: a single honesty constraint compiled into the engine, namely archive pixels are only ever positioned, scaled and masked, never filtered, blurred or graded; and the engine refuses to render a cut from an archive plate to a reconstruction without passing through its label card. The picture is evidence on a flat ground; everything alive is the type, the line, the map and the clock.
titleSequence: About 9 s, skippable, built from the exhibit rule, never a fade-in of a fog. Shared grammar: flat exhibit ground, one archive plate hairline-framed on the grid, title set whole in the exhibit face, catalogue slip (Inter Tight 28px: 'Dossier 02 / Henry Ford and the line / 3 min 40 / Archive photographs ungraded, paintings labelled Reconstruction'). Douglass: silence, then the sound of a type case; letters of FREDERICK DOUGLASS drop into a composing stick as individual sorts on word onsets of the first narration line, spaces stretch to justify the line to the measure, a platen thud pulls an ink proof (gold #d9b36a ink on iron-gall ground, ink squash at letter edges, impression darker at edges), then the 1840s daguerreotype oval is set beneath unretouched. Ford: black, a red-orange #ff4b1f conveyor rule crosses at fixed takt; stencil bin tags (HENRY / FORD / THE LINE) arrive at fixed pitch and punch into place with a time-clock tick; 1863-1947 counter in tabular Anton figures; archive plate rides in on the same rule. Persia: midnight ground, lapis #4f7cff hairline route draws from Seleucia-Ctesiphon eastward while real Syriac (ܥܕܬܐ ܕܡܕܢܚܐ proofed by a native reader) and the Chinese stele heading 大秦景教流行中國碑 sit large and faded behind at legible contrast, Cormorant title fades up on the route, first plate lands. Partition: soot ground, silence, madder #e8553d line is drawn by hand-speed (hesitates, never retreats) across the dark; the title splits along it, one title per side of the line, set in Urdu (Nastaliq), Hindi, Punjabi (Gurmukhi) and English on the same baseline, in turn, 1.2 s each; then the line bends into the map.
typography: Rule: real fonts, real script shaping (DOM text rendered by Chromium, never canvas fillText for Arabic-script, Syriac or Indic), tabular figures for every year, one sans for system voice. 1920x1080 frame. Shared: Inter Tight 28px minimum for credits/catalogue slips and the RECONSTRUCTION label (the only tracked caps in the family, 24px, +0.14em, solid block, never smaller); captions Source Serif 4 at 44px, max 2 lines, 34 characters per line. Douglass: Abril Fatface 190px titles, a wood-type slab (Alfa Slab One) 96px for dates and handbill lines, justified lines with real quad/space expansion, ink-gain texture applied to type only (WebGL ink mask), gold #d9b36a on iron-gall. Ford: Anton caps 220px tight, stencil bin-tag numerals in Anton at 120px with a cut-out mask, Courier Prime 28px for ledger credits, red-orange #ff4b1f on iron; no photocopy costume. Persia: Cormorant Garamond 150px title, italic 60px for place names on the route, Noto Sans Syriac (Eastern) and Noto Serif SC at 260-320px behind the plate at about 22% opacity but never overlapping the title, always paired with an English gloss at reading size when first shown; lapis #4f7cff on midnight. Partition: Fraunces 170px titles with soft/wonk off for legibility, Noto Nastaliq Urdu, Noto Sans Devanagari, Noto Sans Gurmukhi at equal size and weight per title, madder #e8553d on soot, uncertainty ranges set in tabular Fraunces. Each script proofed and credited to named native readers on the end card.
captionsAndLowerThirds: Kill the translucent rounded box. Layout: plate on the left two thirds of the grid, largest object; a flat right column holds year, place, and the source slip; a dedicated bottom band (22% of height) holds captions so text can never overlap evidence. Captions are word-synced from narration timestamps (forced alignment of the actual TTS/VO), words brighten from 55% to 100% as spoken (no karaoke colour), two lines max, hold until the next breath. Numbers and names spoken as words in the VO are set as figures in the exhibit's accent colour at the moment they are spoken (1913, 93 minutes, Radcliffe). Credit line is a catalogue slip pinned bottom-left of the plate, 26-28px, 'Archive: Library of Congress, 1855, public domain' in plain text; reconstructions get a solid RECONSTRUCTION block at the plate's top-left corner plus a one-line evidence note under it ('Composition imagined; the kitchen is documented at Greenfield Village'). Captions are also exported as WebVTT for the platform player so the film can run as live DOM text on the exhibit page.
transitions: 1. SORT DROP (Douglass, scene to scene within a chapter): the outgoing caption line is distributed - its letters lift out of the stick in reverse order, 10 frames at 30 fps - while the incoming line is set sort by sort, each letter dropping on its word onset in the narration; plate swaps with a 6-frame hard cut at the platen thud. Timed so the new first word lands within 2 frames of the VO onset. 2. PROOF PULL (Douglass, chapter change): a ragged ink-edged mask built from procedural noise sweeps bottom-to-top like a roller, 20 frames, revealing the next plate; the outgoing plate is never faded, only covered. Used once per chapter, never between plates of the same chapter. 3. TAKT TICK (Ford, every scene): hard-edged one-frame-pitch slide along the conveyor rule, 8 frames, ease-in-out cubic, plate pitch constant across the film; a time-clock tick SFX on the first frame. Counter advances one station per scene so the visitor feels the line's rhythm. The takt never changes except at Willow Run, where pitch is faster by the real ratio. 4. ROAD PAN (Persia, chapter change): camera leaves the plate, the plate scales into a lapis map pin, and the camera travels along the route polyline to the next waypoint with eased speed proportional to the real distance (clamped 1.2-2.4 s); the next plate unfolds from the pin. Within a chapter, scenes use a plain 20-frame cross-dissolve with the Syriac/Chinese script drifting 24px to the left, so script is the only thing that moves. 5. LINE DRAW (Partition): a madder line is drawn across the screen at hand speed (about 1.1 s, with a 6-frame hesitation midway, driven by a recorded-style noise curve), then the incoming plate is revealed on one side of the line only; the outgoing plate remains on the other for 0.6 s before it too is replaced. The line never erases itself; it stays as a 3px hairline in the margin for the rest of the film, thicker each chapter. 6. LABEL GATE (all films, archive to reconstruction): the engine will not compile a direct cut. The archive plate shrinks 12% over 8 frames, the RECONSTRUCTION block slams in at the plate corner with a muted click, the evidence note types on for 20 frames, then the painting is set smaller inside a hairline frame. The reverse (painting to archive) is the plate growing back to full size with the label retracting. This is a rule, not a preference. 7. HELD SILENCE (all films, for gated or distressing material): no animated transition at all. Music drops out 1.0 s before, a hard cut to a plain card in the exhibit face with the content note, 1.5 s hold, then a hard cut to the document or photograph. No ink, no line, no map, no particles for harm. The absence of the engine is the transition.
motionGraphics: Everything is a live rule, not a keyframed illustration. (1) Douglass: the 1845 Narrative title page is set as a type specimen proof - lines of the real title page animate as the VO reads them (WRITTEN BY HIMSELF set last, on the word himself); a literacy line chart is NOT fabricated, only real dated events are set as handbill lines in Alfa Slab One, one per beat. (2) Ford: the 12.5 hours vs 93 minutes graphic is drawn to scale as two bars on one conveyor rule: 750 min vs 93 min, the short bar is 12.4% of the long one, built live from the numbers; Model T count 15 million as a tabular ledger counter ticking by year using real production figures from the cited source, never a made-up curve. (3) Persia: a real vector map (Natural Earth, public domain) with the route as one continuous lapis polyline, each waypoint a pin with year and place in Cormorant italic (Seleucia-Ctesiphon 410, Chang'an 635, stele 781), labelled 'traditional route, approximate'; camera follows the path. (4) Partition: one line drawn on a real district-level base map, with the 1947 boundary line drawn from the Boundary Commission data; the uncertainty bar for deaths is drawn as an honest range (about 200,000 to 2,000,000, historians disagree) with a smeared band and the words 'no one knows', and the 15 million displaced is a single measured bar, never a dot swarm; both gated. (5) Kinetic type moments: max three per film, each tied to a spoken number or date that is the beat of the story (Douglass 1838 and 1845, Ford 93, Persia 635 and 781, Partition 17 August). No kinetic type on suffering; those lines are static captions.

perExhibit.douglass: Composing stick is the rule. Iron-gall ground (#120f0c-#1a1411), gold #d9b36a ink, Abril Fatface plus slab. Every caption is set as a justified line sort by sort on narration; chapter changes are proof pulls. Keep the daguerreotype oval and the Narrative title page ungraded and at true size on the grid, framed by hairlines only; kill the amber fog entirely. The Baltimore engraving gets a flat ground and a handbill date line, not a darkening fade. Faceless reconstructions only (boy chalking a plank, press room without a person); retire painted lectern and study portraits as the council already found. The ink texture lives in the type only, never over a photograph.
perExhibit.ford: The line is the rule: constant pitch, one station per scene, time-clock tick on each cut. Anton caps in #ff4b1f on iron, stencil bin tags for the year counter. The 93-minute vs 12.5-hour bar is the central graphic. Highland Park photograph is the largest plate in the film, shown ungraded with its real edges; painted Ford portraits never appear; back-turned rider on Bagley Avenue stays, labelled. The Beliefs and Morals chapter uses HELD SILENCE then the real Dearborn Independent masthead at the same type size and grammar as the Rouge, no stencil, no red, no engine flourishes; the line simply stops (counter stays at the last station, silent).
perExhibit.persia: The road is the rule. Midnight ground (#0c1020), lapis #4f7cff, Cormorant Garamond with Syriac and Chinese script large, legible and faded behind each plate, with English gloss. One continuous route from Ctesiphon to Chang'an; camera travels it at chapter changes. Seal and stele plates stay ungraded; paintings (vault at Ctesiphon, bishops' hall, stele court) shrink into a hairline frame with label gate; no amber glow, no lamps on the manuscript. Martyrdom chapter: HELD SILENCE, plain card, no map, no motion. The Chinese and Syriac must be proofed by named native readers before render.
perExhibit.partition: The map line is the rule. Soot ground, madder #e8553d, Fraunces plus Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi and English titles on one baseline, equal weight. The line is drawn in hand-speed at the title and stays as a margin hairline that thickens each chapter. Real photographs primary and ungraded; no painted figures; Reconstruction only for places or empty rooms. Violence, mass death and refugee-column material is gated and handled with HELD SILENCE and a content card; the casualty uncertainty bar is the only graphic on that subject and carries no animation beyond a single static draw. End card names the Urdu, Hindi and Punjabi proofreaders.

soundTies: All motion is clocked to the narration, not the other way round: forced-alignment word timestamps (JSON) are the master clock. Rule: caption words brighten on word onset; sorts, bin tags and route pins land on the first word of the sentence they illustrate, within 2 frames at 30 fps; chapter-change transitions start on the sentence-final breath (the pause detected in the alignment, min 250 ms) and end on the next sentence onset, so nothing covers a spoken word. Score is sidechain-ducked 6 dB under the VO and its envelope drives only the small things (conveyor speed jitter +/- 3%, ink gain on type, route glow); it never drives the evidence. Diegetic SFX only: type-case rattle and platen thud (Douglass), time-clock tick and conveyor hum at takt (Ford), footfall and wind bed on the route (Persia), a single pen scratch and room tone (Partition). Every gated passage: music out 1.0 s before, no SFX. The same JSON drives the WebVTT captions and the chapter list on the platform player.
productionMethod: Build one Plate Engine as a single HTML page (DOM for text so Chromium does real Urdu, Syriac, Devanagari, Gurmukhi and CJK shaping; SVG for route/line/map paths; WebGL only for ink mask and the type-only texture), deterministic via window.__t clock and a per-film seed, driven by narration alignment JSON plus a scene manifest (plate, kind=archive|reconstruction, region-of-interest boxes, credit, evidence note, gated flag). Playwright steps t frame by frame at 1920x1080, 30 fps, screenshots to PNG; ffmpeg encodes (ProRes mezzanine, then H.264 CRF 16 for web) with the VO and score muxed; WebVTT written from the same alignment. Archive plates: highest-resolution source scans (LoC/Wikimedia TIFF) used as-is; no AI upscaling of evidence (that is processing). Camera moves only along authored regions of interest in time with the narration, not a generic 2% dolly. Pillow: pre-cutting plate margins and contact-sheet QA only. Lottie/dotLottie: small repeated ornaments only (RECONSTRUCTION block slam, hairline tick), reused across films. Magnific: spend credits on sound effects (audio_sfx_generate for case rattle, time-clock tick) and, if the owner wants, regenerated faceless reconstructions to the shared art-direction sheet; no generative video of real people, no generative graphics. Fabula: assemble the final audio mix, chapter markers and captions track; Tela: static title cards and the lobby posters from the same tokens. Ship two outputs: a baked MP4 for TV/offline and the live Plate Engine composition for the exhibit page, which runs from the same manifest.
risk: Four bespoke rule systems is real engineering and an owner who wants 'cinematic' may see flat grounds, hairlines and thin plates as austere or a template with nice type. Determinism makes the baked film identical every time; that is honest, but the live version must not pretend to be unique per viewer for effect. Failure modes I will police: kinetic type drifting into spectacle on Beliefs, martyrdom, Partition violence; mis-shaped Urdu, Syriac or Gurmukhi from a font fallback (must be proofed by native readers); a route or boundary map presented as more precise than the sources (labelled approximate); the engine's flat ground reading cold next to the warm photographs. Frame-by-frame rendering of about 4 films at 3-4 minutes is around 28,000 frames each and will need caching of plate textures and parallel workers.

arguesWith.why: CINEMATIC will want a unified filmic grade, anamorphic letterbox, grain and slow push-ins to make these feel expensive. That is the current failure in another form: the Douglass fog, the amber Persia wash and the 2% drift are a look laid over evidence, not a behaviour the material causes. I will give them camera moves only where a rule or the narration points at a region of interest (the face, the title line, the chassis), photographs are never graded, and the 'cinema' is rhythm, timing against the VO and honest silence, not a LUT. A held ungraded photograph with a precise word landing on it is more filmic than a blurred glow.
